question: What follows if valid cognition is identified with its total causal complex?
premises: Some identify valid cognition with the totality of its causal factors.
By doing so they clearly accept the cognitive status of the object and other factors.
If that status belongs to the aggregate, it cannot be denied to its members without explanation.
inference: Treating the causal aggregate as valid cognition implicitly grants cognitive status to the object and related factors.
plain_english: But those who say valid cognition is the totality of its factors clearly accept the cognitive status of the object and so on; if that status belongs even to the aggregate, how could it be otherwise?
